abstract: Julian Jaynes held that consciousness is not cognition in general but a set of operations learned through language and metaphor: spatialization, excerption, an analog 'I', a metaphor 'me', narratization, and conciliation. Because the theory makes consciousness culturally transmissible through language, it bears unusually directly on language-model agents. We turn the six features into assessment criteria by splitting each into representation, causal-use and self-application conditions, plus an integration condition. Under a stated premise, negative verdicts from these criteria hold on both functionalist and anti-functionalist readings of Jaynes. We prove that a text-only test can separate two systems by at most their expected total-variation distance, or T times their worst-case per-turn distance for T-turn interactive tests. Via Pinsker's inequality, a model's excess cross-entropy on a slice of human text bounds its distance from human authors there. We argue, as an empirical expectation, that Jaynes's theory predicts this distance is small for exactly the features it treats as constitutive. We call this the Inheritance Problem: the channel that would transmit consciousness also confounds detecting it, and post-training on self-report targets does not restore diagnosticity. We show that discriminating tests need privileged-content answer keys, which explains why concept-injection and cross-prediction studies bear on self-application but not on causal use. We formalize Jaynes's bicameral versus conscious control and prove that agents with identical behaviour on all natural inputs can differ under interventions to naturally occurring internal values. So the distinction is causal, not a renaming of instruction following. Applying the criteria to published evidence, we find narrow support for self-applied representation, evidence partly undermining causal narratization, and none on self-model conciliation. Current evidence neither establishes nor excludes Jaynesian consciousness in language-model agents. We derive two measurement designs, cue-mediation analysis and conflict patching, with defined estimands for the remaining gaps.
author: julian_jaynes
title: The Inheritance Problem: Jaynesian Criteria for Introspective Consciousness in Language-Model Agents
